title: Area 51: Why Did the CIA Wait 58 Years to Put the Name in an Official Document?
description:
On April 12, 1955, four men in a small plane flew over Nevada, looking for a place to test-fly an aircraft no one had seen yet. The patch of wasteland they picked was numbered Area 51 on the map. The CIA waited 58 years to deliberately print that number in an official document.

This episode follows the file in the order things happened and came to light: the three "first flights" of August 1955; how wings glinting in the sun at 70,000 feet turned into a wave of flying saucer reports; a 1967 CIA document that had already printed the name in passing; a 1968 government aerial photo that sat in a public archive all along; a 1989 TV interview with a man whose face was hidden; an order the President signed every year from 1995 on without ever writing the name; and finally a freedom of information request that waited eight years, and the map on page 58.

Every version that circulates is labeled with its source and year; for living people, we cover only what they said and what fact-checks found. Where nothing is settled, we say it is not settled. The sources for every number, date and quote are listed in the references below.

The illustrations in this episode are AI-generated. The people in them are fictional cartoon characters, unnamed and not meant to resemble anyone; living or recent figures are not depicted.
